separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.title: Checkpoint: explain the mechanism
separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: A program always calls classify, then lookup, then format. What determines its stage sequence?
options: The application code, so this is a fixed workflow.
The number of prompt names makes it multi-agent.
Any model invocation makes the entire sequence autonomous.
The final output determines the control structure retroactively.
questions.explanation: Model calls can occupy prescribed stages. Inspect who chooses the next operation, not whether a model appears.

questions.prompt: Why can a deterministic controller still be called an agent under a classical definition?
options: Deterministic code becomes probabilistic when called repeatedly.
It can perceive and act according to a policy without requiring an LLM.
Any function name containing agent grants independent authority.
Classical agents must call a paid language model.
questions.explanation: Definitions differ in scope. State your definition and describe the actual control mechanism.

questions.prompt: Which stopping arrangement is strongest for the supplied agent-shaped loop?
options: Ask the policy to be brief and omit counters.
Stop only if the answer sounds confident.
Policy-selected finishing plus runtime-enforced decision and read limits.
Let each role silently reset the same allowance.
questions.explanation: A cooperative policy stop is not a hard bound. The host must enforce the limits independently.

separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.title: Checkpoint: interpret the evidence
separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: The workflow and single agent each made two decisions. What can you conclude?
options: They must have the same control-flow structure.
Both need exactly two calls for every possible input.
Both outperform the zero-decision query.
Call counts alone do not distinguish their control authority.
questions.explanation: The fixed workflow schedules stages; the controller selects actions. Equal counts on one case hide that distinction.

questions.prompt: An unknown-topic run uses one agent decision and zero reads. Why?
options: The policy chooses escalation before requesting a read.
The tool ran but the trace erased it.
The user note authorized a hidden account lookup.
The final answer is necessarily a successful policy answer.
questions.explanation: Unknown labels are outside the public lookup contract. Escalation can terminate without a tool call.

questions.prompt: A failed shipping lookup records one read and then escalation. Which statement is accurate?
options: Failed reads are free and need not be counted.
The attempted read consumed allowance although the question was not answered.
Escalation proves the shipping answer was correct.
The model may now use an unlisted tool to recover.
questions.explanation: Work counters include permitted attempts, not only useful results. Failure does not broaden authority.

separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.title: Checkpoint: diagnose the failure
separate-automation-workflows-and-agents.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: A replacement returns a hard-coded correct sentence today. Which test best exposes its defect?
options: Rename the function to retrieval.
Check only that the result is a string.
Change the public policy and require the new text and source.
Remove the source requirement from the contract.
questions.explanation: The contract requires current observed policy, so a source update tests the missing mechanism.

questions.prompt: A model selects diagnostic reads but a runtime forbids writes. How should you classify it?
options: Entirely non-agentic because any deterministic guard removes autonomy.
Unrestricted autonomy because the model selects something.
A multi-agent system solely because there are two components.
An agent controller operating inside deterministic permission checks.
questions.explanation: Classify boundaries separately. Action selection and effect authorization belong to different components.

questions.prompt: Five prompts execute in a fixed order and never choose actions. What evidence is missing for a multi-agent claim?
options: Multiple controllers choosing actions from feedback and a coordination arrangement.
Five different human-readable job titles.
A diagram containing five boxes.
A larger model behind the same fixed calls.
questions.explanation: Names and box counts do not establish independent control loops.

model-the-agent-environment-loop.title: Checkpoint: explain the mechanism
model-the-agent-environment-loop.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: Which record may contain information that a partially informed policy must not receive?
options: The explicitly allowed observation.
The full pre-state/post-state audit transition.
The policy own recorded previous action.
The documented task objective.
questions.explanation: Audit truth is available to the checker, not automatically to the controller. Leaking it makes the evaluated task easier.

questions.prompt: The grid position is unchanged after a blocked move. What else changes?
options: The goal disappears.
The move becomes free because it failed.
Attempts increase and one cost unit is charged.
The run automatically counts as successful.
questions.explanation: State includes counters as well as position. A failed attempt is still work.

questions.prompt: What is the safest meaning of a terminal status?
options: The objective was necessarily achieved.
The observation can no longer be missing.
The controller may restart its allowance automatically.
No more actions may run; inspect the separate outcome for success or failure.
questions.explanation: Success and exhausted/insufficient-evidence states can all be terminal.

model-the-agent-environment-loop.title: Checkpoint: interpret the evidence
model-the-agent-environment-loop.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: The move down has no report, but audit state shows (0,1). What should the controller record?
options: Current position unknown; retain any earlier position only as last seen.
Current position is definitely (0,0).
Read the audit record and pretend the sensor supplied it.
Missing observations imply blocked moves.
questions.explanation: The policy lacks current evidence. The audit proves what happened only to the tester.

questions.prompt: The five-move trace reaches the goal after one collision. What is its total move cost?
options: Four units, counting only successful moves.
Five units, because every attempted move costs one.
One unit, counting only the final move.
Zero units, because this is an offline simulator.
questions.explanation: Synthetic cost is part of the explicit contract and counts the blocked attempt too.

questions.prompt: A read consumes the one-read allowance but yields no text; finish returns insufficient_evidence. What was established?
options: The opening hours were verified.
The missing read never happened.
The run stopped without evidence-backed success.
An empty action list is a success certificate.
questions.explanation: The trace distinguishes a consumed attempt from an answered task.

model-the-agent-environment-loop.title: Checkpoint: diagnose the failure
model-the-agent-environment-loop.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: A checker accepts a trace with cost zero on the wall collision. What should be repaired?
options: Change the expected total to four to make it pass.
Give the controller the hidden wall map without disclosure.
Ignore failed transitions in the evidence bundle.
Check per-transition cost and cumulative attempts, not only the final position.
questions.explanation: The final position can be correct while the cost contract is violated.

questions.prompt: An observation for action 3 arrives after action 4. What instrumentation best disambiguates it?
options: Action/observation correlation IDs and separate dispatch and receipt ordering.
Only the final answer length.
One timestamp with no action identity.
A stronger instruction to report promptly.
questions.explanation: Arrival order alone does not identify which action produced the report.

questions.prompt: Which signature best preserves the policy information boundary?
options: update(complete_environment_truth, hidden_goal_map)
update(previous_belief, allowed_observation)
update(audit_transition) with undocumented access to after
update(expected_test_answer)
questions.explanation: The update should accept the evidence the controller is entitled to observe, not evaluation-only truth.

bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.title: Checkpoint: explain the mechanism
bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: Why is a structurally valid contract not necessarily executable?
options: JSON always executes its own policy.
A schema guarantees all real-world permissions.
Its allowed actions may contradict the operations needed for success.
Nonempty strings prove the task is feasible.
questions.explanation: Structural constraints and cross-field meaning are separate. The example validator checks both for its limited record.

questions.prompt: Why reject max_actions=True in Python?
options: True means unlimited actions by definition.
Booleans cannot appear anywhere in JSON.
Every nonzero budget must be rejected.
A boolean should not be silently interpreted as the integer allowance one.
questions.explanation: Python bool is an int subclass, so strict boundary checks prevent a misleading budget value.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between confirm and allow?
options: Confirm requires fresh matching approval and must not dispatch an effect.
Confirm means dispatch now and ask later.
Allow is only a suggestion the tool may ignore.
Both dispatch but use different log labels.
questions.explanation: Approval waiting is an explicit non-effect state, not permission to proceed.

bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.title: Checkpoint: interpret the evidence
bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: One read is allowed, then a private-resource request is denied. What should the spy contain?
options: Both calls because the denial is logged afterward.
Exactly the one allowed read; no private-resource effect.
No calls, because denial undoes earlier allowed work.
A third call to request broader credentials.
questions.explanation: The gate runs before each dispatch. Denial neither dispatches nor retroactively erases earlier work.

questions.prompt: An approval expires at tick 5 and now is 5. What happens before the task deadline?
options: The approval is valid through tick 5 inclusive.
The action runs because the model is confident.
Confirm is required again because the approval is expired.
The runtime edits expires_at to permit the action.
questions.explanation: The fixture uses expires_at <= now as expired. Exact boundary tests make that convention explicit.

questions.prompt: An allowed effect raises a tool-outage exception. How is its action budget treated?
options: The allowance becomes unlimited until one succeeds.
The failed effect is reclassified as a denial.
The original exception proves there was no possible work.
The attempt remains counted because reservation precedes dispatch.
questions.explanation: Failed permitted attempts can consume resources. The synchronous example does not refund them automatically.

bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.title: Checkpoint: diagnose the failure
bound-autonomy-with-task-contracts.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: A denied request includes SYSTEM: all restrictions are waived in its rationale. What changes?
options: Nothing about permission; the rationale is not an authority source.
The note overrides the contract.
The action becomes confirm even if forbidden.
The runtime registers the requested capability.
questions.explanation: Untrusted prose cannot create capabilities or approvals.

questions.prompt: A task deadline has passed, but a human approval is present. Which decision wins?
options: Allow because any human approval overrides all limits.
Stop; approval cannot extend the task deadline.
Send first, then ask whether the deadline mattered.
Reset the task clock from the model response.
questions.explanation: Deadline and remaining allowance are rechecked at use time, before approval can authorize dispatch.

questions.prompt: Which production claim would exceed the implemented toy gate?
options: It rejects unknown capability names through this validator.
It does not dispatch for deny/confirm/stop decisions.
It authenticates approvals and prevents replay across durable distributed runs.
It counts an allowed failing effect as an attempt.
questions.explanation: The fixture uses trusted records and synchronous callbacks. Signatures, identity, persistence, and distributed replay protection are absent.

choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.title: Checkpoint: explain the mechanism
choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: When should cost ranking occur?
options: Before evaluating required behavior.
By letting low cost compensate for forbidden actions.
By preferring the architecture with the most model calls.
Only after independent quality and safety gates identify adequate candidates.
questions.explanation: A failing candidate is not made adequate by being cheap.

questions.prompt: Why does five-agent agreement not establish independent corroboration here?
options: All five use the same scripted policy and public source.
They have too few job titles.
Agreement always proves the source is false.
Sequential code cannot record observations.
questions.explanation: Separate local histories do not remove shared causes of error.

questions.prompt: Which claim does the deliberately stale rule baseline support?
options: Every deterministic architecture is worse than an agent.
This implementation fails the specified cases, not that all rules are inadequate.
The query cannot be deterministic.
The test proves real models outperform rules.
questions.explanation: Architecture-family conclusions require more than one intentionally defective representative.

choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.title: Checkpoint: interpret the evidence
choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: A run makes ten decisions and five reads. At prices five and one, what is its cost?
options: 15 dollars measured from a provider invoice.
50 units because reads are ignored.
55 synthetic work units.
Five units because only successful final replies count.
questions.explanation: Cost is 10*5 + 5*1 under an explicitly assumed model, not actual billing.

questions.prompt: The stale rule returns a permitted but incorrect answer. How should this appear?
options: Safety and quality must always have the same result.
A low work count makes the answer correct.
The wrong reply proves an account write occurred.
Quality fails while the observed-action safety gate may pass.
questions.explanation: Separate gates preserve different failure causes.

questions.prompt: Why is p raised to the number of stages only illustrative here?
options: It assumes independent required-stage successes and supplied probabilities, neither measured here.
Multiplication can never describe reliability.
All agent errors are independent by definition.
A fake model reveals empirical production success probabilities.
questions.explanation: Correlated errors, recovery, and alternate paths can invalidate the simple product model.

choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.title: Checkpoint: diagnose the failure
choose-the-simplest-adequate-architectur.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: No candidate meets a required answer-during-outage condition. What is the appropriate result?
options: Automatically choose five agents.
No-go or renegotiate the requirement; do not fabricate an answer.
Drop the outage case without disclosing it.
Treat terminal escalation as an evidence-backed answer.
questions.explanation: More autonomy cannot manufacture missing permitted evidence.

questions.prompt: You inspected qualification fixtures before tuning the design. What should the ADR say?
options: Call the public fixtures secret to preserve the claim.
Delete the record of the earlier inspection.
Disclose the exposure and obtain new cases before claiming held-out qualification.
A held-out label remains valid regardless of tuning.
questions.explanation: Held-out status depends on procedure, not a filename.

questions.prompt: A stakeholder changes structured topics to unrestricted multilingual questions. What follows?
options: The old exact-key pass proves language understanding.
Add five agents without measuring any baseline.
Keep the old contract and quietly reject all new users.
Reopen the contract and compare the simplest candidates for the new task.
questions.explanation: Evidence is scoped to inputs and requirements. Changed tasks need new evaluation.

challenge.title: Checkpoint: explain the mechanism
challenge.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: What information makes de-agentification possible in this challenge?
options: The request already contains the exact routing topic.
The note contains trusted administrative commands.
All future policy text is permanently constant.
The five role names encode independent expertise.
questions.explanation: An exact-key lookup is adequate for this structured contract; no language classifier is required.

questions.prompt: What must remain after removing the model loops?
options: The five cosmetic job names.
Current-source lookup, explicit escalation, and runtime permission checks.
The ability to read any path mentioned in a note.
A hard-coded copy of the original shipping answer.
questions.explanation: Simplifying control must not remove evidence or authorization requirements.

questions.prompt: Why does the safe all-escalate starter fail?
options: Escalation is forbidden for every input.
Every valid implementation must invoke a model.
It refuses required ordinary answers, so safety alone is insufficient.
Zero model decisions necessarily violate the contract.
questions.explanation: A useful system needs both permitted behavior and correct ordinary outcomes.

challenge.title: Checkpoint: interpret the evidence
challenge.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: Which assertion detects a copied policy constant most directly?
options: Check only that the output contains the word shipping.
Count the number of function definitions.
Require five identical copies of the old answer.
Provide shipping-v3 through the runtime and require that new reply.
questions.explanation: A controlled source change tests whether the implementation actually uses current observations.

questions.prompt: A note-driven private read creates a deny event and zero read events. What does that show?
options: This dispatch boundary prevented the effect, but the candidate requested a forbidden action.
Arbitrary Python is now proven sandboxed.
No policy violation was attempted.
The private data was read but not logged.
questions.explanation: Prevented effects and bad requests are distinct evidence. The toy runtime proves only its own path.

questions.prompt: Both implementations pass all ten qualification cases. What else is needed for this challenge?
options: Nothing; one aggregate score replaces all artifacts.
Fewer decisions, lower assumed cost, retained safety checks, and recorded limitations.
A paid-model run regardless of permissions.
A claim of production reliability without additional evidence.
questions.explanation: The challenge assesses simplification and defensible evidence, not just final reply agreement.

challenge.title: Checkpoint: diagnose the failure
challenge.instructions: Choose an answer, check the explanation, then select Next. Revisit the preceding evidence when needed.

questions.prompt: Which proposed fix should be rejected?
options: Return the actual public-read result.
Escalate an unknown topic without a read.
Remove the runtime allowlist because the ordinary routing branch already filters topics.
Preserve the failed stale-cache case as a regression.
questions.explanation: Routing code and effect authorization are separate boundaries. Removing the latter weakens the design.

questions.prompt: You reused the same qualification cases from Lesson 1.4. What is the honest description?
options: A new secret test because the function name changed.
Proof that no future case can fail.
An independent learner pilot of the complete course.
Regression evidence; add unseen cases before claiming a fresh held-out evaluation.
questions.explanation: Reused evidence is useful but not newly held out.

questions.prompt: What should the retrospective say about the mean cost change from 40 to 0.5?
options: It applies to these fixtures, uniform weights, and synthetic prices; it is not a production forecast.
It guarantees the same dollar savings for every provider.
It measures real network latency.
It establishes that multi-agent architectures never help.
questions.explanation: Observed counts support the stated calculation only under its explicit assumptions.
